# Game model (ARC-style mirror-maze, 6 levels)

## Core rules (verified L1)
- Board is a square grid of equal cells (L1: 10x10, 40px cells, origin x=72,y=72).
  Determine cell size/origin each level by pixel reading; features align to cell boundaries.
- BLACK = walkable corridor. Solid background color (2 tones, left/right halves) = wall.
- Two cyan agents: A in left half, B in right half.
- Every action moves BOTH agents one cell; an agent whose target cell is wall/off-board stays put.
  - ACTION1 = both UP, ACTION2 = both DOWN
  - ACTION3 = A LEFT, B RIGHT  (horizontal is MIRRORED for B)
  - ACTION4 = A RIGHT, B LEFT
- GOAL: make the two agents occupy the SAME cell -> level completes.
- Useful invariant: s = A.col + B.col is unchanged by horizontal moves unless exactly one agent
  is blocked (then s changes by 1). Merging needs s even AND same row. Vertical moves never change s.
- Halves are usually connected only through a narrow bridge (L1: the top row), so plan the crossing.

## Method that worked
1. read_pixels a full 64x64 map, then a cell-center grid read to get the corridor map exactly.
2. Model as (A,B) state search; use walls to break symmetry (blocked moves change s / row offset).
3. Verify each action's predicted result against the returned image.

## Unknowns
- ACTION5 / ACTION6 (coordinate click) have no observed use yet.
- L2 introduces red/black checkered patches (unknown: hazard or one-way/breakable?).

# Game model (mirror-maze co-op, 6 levels)

## Core rules (verified L1-L5)
- Square grid; determine cell size/origin per level by pixel reading (features align to cells).
- BLACK = corridor; solid 2-tone background = wall.
- Two cyan agents, one per half. EVERY action moves BOTH; a blocked agent stays put.
  ACTION1 = both UP, ACTION2 = both DOWN.
  Horizontal is MIRRORED between the agents, but WHICH action is which can differ per level:
  L1-L4: ACTION3 = A left / B right. L5: ACTION3 = A right / B left. TEST ONE MOVE to fix the mapping.
- GOAL each level: both agents in the SAME cell (they can arrive together from opposite sides,
  or one walks into the other while that one is blocked).
- Blocking is the only way to break mirror symmetry: s = A.col + B.col is invariant under
  horizontal moves unless exactly one agent is blocked; vertical moves never change s.
  Merge needs same row and A.col = B.col.

## Objects
- RED/BLACK CHECKERED cells: impassable (act as walls; never entered - treat as hazard).
- BLUE small square (drawn smaller than the cell): movable BLOCK.
  ACTION6 click on it = select (turns yellow, agents freeze/white); ACTION1-4 then move the BLOCK
  one cell in the literal (non-mirrored) direction; ACTION6 on any other cell = deselect.
  Use blocks as walls-on-demand (e.g., a vertical blocker to fix a row offset), or clear passages.
- FULL-CELL COLORED bars/cells (green/orange/purple...): DOORS and KEYS of that color.
  A lone colored cell = KEY = pressure plate: while an agent STANDS on it, all same-colored
  door-bars (located in the OTHER half) are removed; stepping off restores them.
  Keys are walkable; doors/bars are not; neither is selectable or pushable.
  TRICK: an agent standing INSIDE a doorway when the bar restores stays there and becomes
  pinned horizontally - useful to keep an agent in a door column while the partner walks.
- ACTION5: no observed effect in any level.

## Method
1. read_pixels 64x64 for the whole board, then a cell-center grid read to get the exact map.
2. Work in mirrored coordinates (B' = (r, maxc - B.c)) so both agents move identically.
3. Plan with blocking (walls, edges, blocks, doorway pinning) to fix row offsets and column sums.
4. Predict each action's effect and verify against the returned image.

## Core rules (verified L1-L6)

  on the same tick its partner steps off the key; the bar then restores AROUND the agent, pinning
  it horizontally (it can still move vertically). This "doorway pinning" is a key technique.

# Mirror-maze co-op puzzle — SOLVED (6/6, WIN at turn 256)

## Core rules (verified across all 6 levels)
- Square grid; find cell size/origin per level by pixel reading (features align to cells).
- BLACK = corridor; solid 2-tone background = wall.
- Two cyan agents (one per half). EVERY action moves BOTH; a blocked agent stays put.
  ACTION1 = both UP, ACTION2 = both DOWN.
  Horizontal is MIRRORED between agents, but which action is "A left" VARIES BY LEVEL
  (L1-L4, L6: ACTION3 = A left / B right; L5: reversed). Always test one move first.
- GOAL: get both agents into the SAME cell (arrive together from opposite sides, or one walks
  into the other while that one is blocked).
- Invariant: s = A.col + B.col is unchanged by horizontal moves unless exactly one agent is
  blocked; vertical moves never change s. Row offsets change only via blocked vertical moves.
  => In a perfectly mirror-symmetric region, agents stay mirrored; you MUST use an asymmetry
  (wall, door state, or a movable block) to desync them.

## Hazards / objects
- RED-CHECKERED cells are LETHAL: pushing an agent in restarts the level. They do not block.
  Check both agents' target cells before every press.
- Safe blockers: solid walls, closed colored door-bars, blue blocks, board edges (non-red).
- BLUE BLOCK (drawn smaller than its cell): ACTION6 click = select (turns yellow, agents freeze);
  ACTION1-4 then move that block one cell in the LITERAL direction; ACTION6 elsewhere = deselect.
  Blocks cannot enter walls or key cells. Use them as portable, safe blockers.
- Full-cell COLORED bars = doors; a lone colored cell = KEY (walkable pressure plate).
  Same-colored doors are removed ONLY WHILE an agent stands on the key (keys sit in the
  opposite half from their doors).
- Move resolution uses the door state from the START of the tick: an agent can enter a doorway
  on the same tick its partner steps off the key; the bar then restores AROUND it, pinning it
  horizontally while it can still move vertically ("doorway pinning") — essential in L5 and L6.
- ACTION5: no observed effect anywhere.

## Winning method
1. read_pixels 64x64 for the layout, then a cell-center grid read for the exact map.
2. Identify the single connection(s) between halves; the merge usually happens there.
3. Plan in mirrored coordinates; use blocked moves to build the needed row offset / column sum.
4. Verify each predicted position against the returned image before continuing.

[After action · message]
**Game complete — WIN (6/6 levels).**

Final level's solution chain, for the record:
1. Both agents stepped on their keys, opening both bars simultaneously.
2. With the agents frozen, I drove the blue block up through the open green doorway and parked it at (2,4) — the only source of asymmetry in an otherwise perfectly mirrored board.
3. That block let agent A be held in place (blocked from below/right) while B descended, creating the row offset that was otherwise mathematically impossible.
4. A tapped the orange key so B could slip into the doorway on the exact tick A stepped off; the bar restored around B, pinning it, and B dropped into the bottom-right room.
5. The block was relocated to (5,4) as a safe wall so A could sit at (5,3) while B crossed the bridge to the green key.
6. A entered the green doorway, dropped into the bottom-left room, and the two closed the final gap using the restored green bar as a blocker.

Key discoveries that made it work: keys are hold-to-open pressure plates, moves resolve against the door state at the start of the tick (enabling "doorway pinning"), blue blocks are portable safe walls — and, learned the hard way, red-checkered cells are lethal rather than blocking.
